answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring proof of unique hardware: each agent presents an attestation from a trusted execution environment bound to one physical device, one identity per chip. A sybil operator cloning ten thousand fake agents must buy ten thousand devices, the cost being hardware plus a per-identity attestation fee. Honest agents pay once for their real machine, while the attacker's expense grows until it stops paying. When margins hit a nadir, only genuine hardware earns its keep, and each clone burns out like a comet instead of enduring like quartz.
